annotations.title: Weigh one action against a named policy

description: Call this when you are about to DO something and need one answer you can act on: pay an address, connect to an MCP server, call a tool, or put capital into a vault. The answer depends on the AMOUNT, the ACTION, the POLICY you name and how much we actually read — so the same address can be `allow` for $5 and `abstain` for $5,000. Four decisions. `allow` means nothing we could check objects, up to `maxAmountUsd`, and is NOT a statement that the action is safe: nothing here sees what it is for or what you agreed. `review` means something we READ does not match, and `reasons` names which rule. `abstain` means we did not read enough to have an opinion — our gap, never approval. `unsupported` means the policy has no rule for this action, and inventing one would be worse than declining. Every rule id in `reasons` is published in full at the policies tool, including to the party being evaluated. SINCE 2026-10-11 A POLICY JUDGES THE RISK LEVEL, NOT ONLY ITS TRUSTWORTHINESS. `risk-band-is-supported` asks whether the band survives what we could not read; `risk-band-within-policy` and `controller-risk-within-policy` ask whether the band and the control we DID read are ones this policy will commit capital against. Conservative will not allocate into a band worse than moderate, nor where control is `thin` — one party able to move the money — and returns `review` rather than `abstain`, because a band we read as high is a finding about the vault and not a gap in our reading. Permissive declares neither threshold and is unchanged. This closed a real defect: a vault our own vault_check called high risk with 0.5% withdrawable used to come back `allow`, because every rule about the AVAILABILITY of risk data passed. Free.

action.description: What you are about to do.

amountUsd.description: What you are about to commit, in US dollars. Leave it out and the amount rules report that they did not run, rather than passing.

chain.description: The chain the action settles on, e.g. base, polygon, solana.

policy.description: A policy version or slug. Defaults to conservative-v1. An unknown name is REFUSED rather than silently replaced with the default.

requiredChecks.description: Rule ids YOU will not act without, e.g. ["quoted-payee-matches-proposal","live-price-matches-proposal"]. The policy is OUR view of what matters; this is yours. Any one of them that does not reach a verdict — because we could not read it, or because it never applied to what you sent — turns the answer into ABSTAIN instead of ALLOW. It can only ever make the answer more conservative: a required check that passes changes nothing, and a real objection stays a REVIEW rather than being buried as an abstain. An id we do not hold is NAMED in `required.unknownIds` rather than ignored, because a caller whose requirement was never looked at must not read `allow` as it having been met. `list_policies` has every id.

resource.description: The http(s) endpoint being bought or connected to, where that differs from `subject`. This is what reaches the seller’s own catalogue entry, carrying their price and their payee.

subject.description: What you are about to do it to: an address to pay, an endpoint URL to connect to, or a vault slug.

name: evaluate_action

byArea.description: The same coverage, PER QUESTION: counterparty, payment-intent, service, capital. Read this rather than the single `coverage` when the action moves money. The denominator is the rules the policy holds for that area, NOT the ones that happened to apply — so an area where nothing could be checked reports `none`, which is the fact, instead of reporting high coverage of nothing.

coverage.description: How much of what the policy wanted was actually there. Below the policy floor the decision is `abstain` rather than `allow`.

decision.description: `allow` is not “safe” and `abstain` is not “nothing found”. Read `decisions` in the answer for what each one means.

decisions.description: What each decision word means, so a caller never has to guess. Read it before treating `allow` as approval or `abstain` as a clean result.

limits.description: What a decision here is and is not. `allow` means no rule objected under this policy at this coverage, which is not a statement that the action is safe.

maxAmountUsd.description: The most this policy permits for this proposal. Null where the action moves no money, and null on anything but an `allow`, because a limit printed beside a `review` reads as permission.

missingEvidence.description: Rule ids whose evidence we do not hold. These lower `coverage` and are NEVER counted as objections.

notApplicable.description: Rules this PROPOSAL does not raise, each with `why` and what to send to have it checked. Distinct from `missingEvidence`, which is a gap in our record: a payment naming no `resource` has no listing to be found in, so those rules do not apply and do not lower coverage. Send `resource` and two more checks run, both decisive.

paymentIntent.description: Whether this payment was checked against WHAT IT IS BUYING, in one field. `not-verified` means the policy holds such rules and none of them ran, which on a payment is almost always a missing `resource`: the counterparty may have an excellent record and nothing has compared this amount to this service. `verified` means at least one reached a verdict. `not-applicable` means the policy asks nothing about it, or the action is not a payment.

policy.description: The policy applied: its intent, its ceiling and the coverage floor below which it abstains.

policyVersion.description: Carried so an answer given today can be reproduced after the rules change.

proposal.description: What you asked about, read back, so a typo is visible before you act on the answer.

reasons.description: Rule ids that decided. Look them up in the policy to see the sentence each one checks.

required.description: Present only where you sent `requiredChecks`. `met`, `unmet` and `unknownIds`, with a sentence. An `unmet` entry is why the decision is ABSTAIN.

rules.description: Every rule considered, each pass, fail or unknown. The audit trail for the decision.

says.description: The decision in one sentence, naming the rules that drove it. Written to be shown to whoever authorises the action.

title: Weigh one action against a named policy
